title: Programmes and Channels Available to Primary School Students to Learn and Raise the Alert on Domestic Violence
what_it_is: Programmes and Channels Available to Primary School Students to Learn and Raise the Alert on Domestic Violence

sections.label: Primary school personal safety teaching
sections.summary: Primary school students are taught personal safety and how to safeguard themselves against abuse in an age-appropriate manner.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: In Primary schools, students are taught personal safety and how to safeguard themselves against abuse in an age-appropriate manner.

sections.label: Reporting and child abuse procedures
sections.summary: Students can report to Teachers, School Counsellors or Student Welfare Officers, who use the Child Abuse Reporting Guide; Principals report suspected abuse to the Child Protective Service.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Students who face such situations can report them to their Teachers, School Counsellors or Student Welfare Officers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: All School Counsellors and Student Welfare Officers are trained to use the Child Abuse Reporting Guide which was jointly developed by MSF and the Ministries with frontline staff working with children, for MOE, MOH, the Singapore Police Force.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Principals report suspected child abuse cases, including exposure to family violence, immediately to the Child Protective Service, and work closely with the Child Protection Officers and/or Approved Welfare Officers to ensure that timely intervention is provided for the children involved.

sections.label: Primary 1 safety rights lessons
sections.summary: From Primary 1, students are taught about personal rights to safety and safeguarding themselves through mandatory Character and Citizenship Education lessons.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: In Primary schools, students are taught in Primary 1, as young as from Primary 1, about their personal rights to safety and how to safeguard themselves.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: These are lessons which are part of the Character and Citizenship Education.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: These lessons are mandatory for all schools to deliver.

sections.label: Teachers trained on non-verbal cues
sections.summary: Teachers are trained to pick up non-verbal cues, such as drawings suggesting family violence or abuse at home.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Teachers are also trained to pick up these non-verbal cues.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: If young children should, through their drawings, suggest that there are things happening at home that they are not comfortable with, that perhaps suggest family violence or abuse, teachers are trained to pick this up.
